fullPassage: In the 1950s, biologists observed chimpanzees that weren't biologically related sharing meat. They struggled to understand why animals that aren't part of the same family help one another. Today, it is believed that the answer is related to game theory. To understand this concept better, consider the following situation. Tournaments were once held by a political scientist in which computer programs competed against each other. Each program had a specific strategy that it followed when encountering an opponent — cooperating with it, backing down from it, and so on. A strategy emerged over time that was more successful than others: start by being cooperative, and then simply copy your opponents' behavior. In other words, if they cooperate, I cooperate. If they stop sharing with me, I stop sharing with them. The behavior we observe in the animal kingdom that is similar to this is called reciprocity. The chimpanzees share food with others because they believe the other will return the favor.

det.tip: similar(유사한)의 반대는 different(다른). identical은 오히려 유의어

questions.passage:
(A) The mother gently <u>held</u> her sleeping baby in her arms. The room was quiet, and no one wanted to wake the child.

(B) The music festival was <u>held</u> in the city park last summer. Thousands of people came to enjoy the performances.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 held의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: held: (A) (팔로) 안다, 붙잡다  (B) (행사가) 열리다, 개최되다
det.analysis:
① (A) 안다 (B) 개최되다: 아기를 팔로 안았고(held), 대회가 열렸다(were held) ←정답
② (A) 개최되다 (B) 안다: (A) 아기를 '개최했다'? 부적절
③ (A) 안다 (B) 멈추다: (B) 대회를 '멈췄다'? 부적절
④ (A) 개최되다 (B) 붙잡다: (A) 아기를 '개최했다'? 부적절
det.tip: held의 다의어: (사람을) 안다/붙잡다 vs (행사를) 열다/개최하다

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a person, team, or group that competes against you in a contest, game, or argument"

det.korean: partner=동반자 / ally=동맹 / opponent=상대, 적수 / teammate=팀 동료
det.analysis:
① partner: 동반자, 협력자 — 경쟁 상대가 아님
② ally: 동맹, 협력자 — 경쟁 상대가 아님
③ opponent: 시합·게임·논쟁에서 맞서 겨루는 상대 ←정답
④ teammate: 같은 편의 팀 동료 — 경쟁 상대가 아님
det.tip: competes against you(맞서 겨루는) 사람 = opponent(상대, 적수)

questions.passage: The behavior we observe in the animal kingdom that is similar to this is __________ (call) reciprocity.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: call(동사: 부르다) → called(과거분사). is + p.p. 수동태 구문(is called: ~라고 불린다)
det.analysis: call을 과거분사 called로 변환. 'is ______ reciprocity'에서 is(be동사) 뒤에는 과거분사가 와서 수동태(be + p.p.)를 이루므로, '~라고 불린다'는 의미의 called가 필요
det.tip: is + ______ → 수동태(be + p.p.) → called(~라고 불린다)

questions.passage: A strategy emerged over time that was more successful than others: start by being __________ (cooperate), and then simply copy your opponents' behavior.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: cooperate(동사: 협력하다) → cooperative(형용사: 협력적인). be동사(being) 뒤에는 형용사 보어가 필요
det.analysis: cooperate를 형용사 cooperative로 변환. 'start by being ______'에서 being(be동사) 뒤에는 보어로 형용사가 와야 하므로 cooperative가 필요
det.tip: being + 보어 자리 → 형용사 cooperative(협력적인)

questions.passage: In the 1950s, biologists observed chimpanzees that weren't biologically related sharing meat. They struggled to understand why animals that aren't part of the same family help one another. Today, it is believed that the answer is related to game theory. To understand this concept better, consider the following situation. Tournaments were once held by a political scientist in which computer programs competed against each other. Each program had a specific strategy that it followed when encountering an opponent — cooperating with it, backing down from it, and so on. A strategy emerged over time that was more successful than others: start by being cooperative, and then simply copy your opponents' behavior. In other words, if they cooperate, I cooperate. If they stop sharing with me, I stop sharing with them. The behavior we observe in the animal kingdom that is similar to this is called reciprocity. The chimpanzees share food with others because they believe the other will __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: start a fight=싸움을 시작하다 / break the rule=규칙을 어기다 / ignore the group=무리를 무시하다 / return the favor=은혜를 갚다, 보답하다
det.analysis:
① start a fight: 싸움을 시작한다? 먹이를 나누는 이유로 부적절
② break the rule: 규칙을 어긴다? 문맥과 무관
③ ignore the group: 무리를 무시한다? 호혜성과 반대
④ return the favor: 상대가 보답할 것이라 믿기 때문에 먹이를 나눈다 — 호혜성의 핵심 ←정답
det.tip: share food ... because they believe the other will ___ → 보답할 것(return the favor)이라 믿기에

questions.passage: In the 1950s, biologists observed chimpanzees that weren't biologically related sharing meat. They struggled to understand why animals that aren't part of the same family help one another. Today, it is believed that the answer is related to game theory. To understand this concept better, consider the following situation. Tournaments were once held by a political scientist in which computer programs competed against each other. Each program had a specific strategy that it followed when encountering an opponent — cooperating with it, backing down from it, and so on. A strategy emerged over time that was more successful than others: start by being cooperative, and then simply __________. In other words, if they cooperate, I cooperate. If they stop sharing with me, I stop sharing with them. The behavior we observe in the animal kingdom that is similar to this is called reciprocity. The chimpanzees share food with others because they believe the other will return the favor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: copy your opponents' behavior=상대의 행동을 따라 하다 / attack your opponents first=상대를 먼저 공격하다 / hide your true strategy=진짜 전략을 숨기다 / give up the competition=경쟁을 포기하다
det.analysis:
① copy your opponents' behavior: 협력으로 시작한 뒤 상대의 행동을 그대로 따라 한다 — 뒤 문장 'if they cooperate, I cooperate'가 이를 설명 ←정답
② attack your opponents first: 먼저 공격? 협력으로 시작한다는 문맥과 반대
③ hide your true strategy: 전략을 숨긴다? 문맥과 무관
④ give up the competition: 경쟁을 포기한다? 문맥과 무관
det.tip: 뒤 문장(협력엔 협력, 안 나누면 나도 안 나눔)이 곧 상대 행동을 copy(따라 함)하는 것
